quote: Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287 [NRS-484B-287-1c, NRS-484B-287-1d, NRS-484B-287-1e, LVMC-11-30-060-A, LVMC-11-30-060-B], 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B] and 484B.350 [LVMC-11-46-030]: A pedestrian shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

activation.description: Pedestrian leaves curb or other place of safety into an approaching vehicle path.
activation.source_clause: leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle

obligation.description: Do not suddenly enter when the vehicle is too close for its driver to yield.
obligation.source_clause: A pedestrian shall not suddenly leave

exceptions.source_clause: Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287 [NRS-484B-287-1c, NRS-484B-287-1d, NRS-484B-287-1e, LVMC-11-30-060-A, LVMC-11-30-060-B], 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B] and 484B.350 [LVMC-11-46-030]
exceptions.description: Review the cited statutory conditions and original scene before applying this clause.

timing.description: Use the frame bracket for departure and roadway/path entry, with original approaching-vehicle state at that instant.
timing.source_clause: walk or run into the path of a vehicle

judgment_calls_needed.phrase: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
judgment_calls_needed.note: Actual driver capability and statutory impossibility require original vehicle response and independent judgment; a conditional stopping range is an engineering diagnostic.
